slot_note: architecture 3, a re-root into human-factors-ergonomics (anthropometric-design-fit, descriptive) after architecture 2 (urban-regional-science, network-analysis) died at stage 4; the Shires world, its queue survey and its closure replay stay dead
niche: an ambulance service formed from two predecessor services fixing the cab of its 2027 front-line ambulance order by how many of its rostered drivers each shortlisted converter-and-chassis cab would fail to fit, where one converter moves its cab bulkhead forward to lengthen the patient saloon
analyst_test: A strong analyst who places each rostered driver's predicted H-point inside the seat maker's fore-aft range as each converter mounts the seat and checks the predicted eye point against the chassis vision lines, the service's fit method executed on the stated ranges, files the Wrenfold cab on the FD35 chassis as failing the fewest drivers, when Wrenfold's forward bulkhead stops the reclined backrest of its tall drivers before the seat reaches their positions and the Pennick cab on the same chassis fails the fewest.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is the number of drivers each cab fails to fit, which anthropometric design fit estimates by placing each person's predicted driving posture (hip point, back angle, eye point) in the cab's workspace; with patients and beds or pupils and desks in place of drivers and cabs there is no hip point, back angle, sightline or bulkhead to place, and the task stops making sense.

legacy staff numbers from the former southern service carried in the telematics until the driver cards were reissued
telematics card and ignition events in UTC against a shift rota in UK local time across both clock changes
converter drawings dimensioned from the seat reference point on one converter and from the accelerator heel point on the others
a seat maker's sheet in inches beside metric drawings
re-sent telematics batches after modem outages
absence episodes continued across month ends as separate records

world.org_type: a regional ambulance service formed in 2023 from two predecessor ambulance services

driver: An adjustable part is judged against its own stated range, but where it is mounted a fixed structure behind it stops it short of that range at a point set by each user's own posture, so a count of the users it can serve has to place each user's whole posture against the surrounding structure, and the option with the longest stated range loses exactly the users who need its far end.
driver_concrete: Each shortlisted ambulance cab's count of rostered drivers it fails to fit, where Wrenfold moves its bulkhead forward to lengthen the saloon, so the backrest set at each tall driver's predicted back angle meets the bulkhead before the seat reaches the driver's predicted hip point, which removes the advantage of its longer seat travel; not the drivers outside the seat maker's fore-aft range, nor that range with the vision zone.
stump: A competent analyst places each rostered driver's predicted hip point in the seat maker's fore-aft range as each converter mounts it, checks the predicted eye point against the chassis vision lines and files the Wrenfold cab on the FD35 chassis as failing the fewest drivers; the step that lands it there is taking the seat's stated travel as usable when Wrenfold's forward bulkhead stops the backrest of its tall drivers short of their positions, so the Pennick cab on the FD35 chassis fails the fewest.

differentiation.task258: task258 moves units across a threshold through a step each unit's served document must carry; here no intervention moves anything: each driver's predicted posture is placed against a fixed structure behind an adjustable seat, and the cab with the longest stated travel loses the drivers who need its far end
differentiation.task303: task303 credits an intervention with a shared upstream loss every unit logs; here the decisive relation is geometric, a reclined backrest meeting a bulkhead at a point each driver's own torso angle sets, with no shared record or upstream source
differentiation.task256: task256 carries a reference survey to a population known only by stature and weight to fill a box of ranges; here every driver is measured, every stated range is already met on paper, and the miss is the structure behind the seat stopping the backrest short of each tall driver's position

lineage.driver: A queue held by a stoppage can only leave as fast as the next control downstream lets it through, so where that control sits close enough for the released queue to fill the space between them, each stoppage costs far more than a release at the road's own capacity implies, and the cost has to be built through the downstream control's recorded opening periods rather than from the stoppage and the arrivals alone.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each crossing's closure delay is each counted vehicle's extra time to reach the far count site; at Mill Lane both directions' queues pass the single-track river bridge 42 metres beyond the crossing only in its fixed-time shuttle greens, with seven vehicles of storage between the two stop lines, which lifts Mill Lane's closure delay from 5,000 to 10,000 vehicle-hours and puts it ahead of Station Road's 7,000.
lineage.stump: A competent solver releases each closure's queue at 1,800 vehicles an hour per lane once the barriers rise and names Station Road; the step that lands it there is releasing Mill Lane's queues at the road's own rate when the river bridge's shuttle signals 42 metres on pass each direction only in its own green.
